newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh leader urges non-interference in Afghan war.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader urges non-interference in Afghan war.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev, speaking ahead of a special summit of five former Soviet republics, urged other countries on Friday not to interfere in the internal affairs of war-weary Afghanistan.

Nazarbayev said Kazakhstan was ready to offer its own peace initiative at the meeting, called to mull steps to prevent Afghan fighting from spilling over to Central Asian members of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
"Unfortunately the interests of many great states are focused there (in Afghanistan)," he said. "Now what is important is not to meddle in the internal affairs."

The seizure of the Afghan capital Kabul by the radical Islamic Taleban militia last week and Taleban's advance north towards CIS borders, some of them guarded with Russian help, has worried Moscow and some other states in the region.
Leaders of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and two of Afghanistan's neighbours -- Tajikistan and Uzbekistan -- will join the summit. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is due to head the Russian delegation.
Moscow and its allies in the loose 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States have kept silent so far about how they could strenghten security.
But Nazarbayev said only Kazkhstan was in a position to offer a proper peace proposal for Afghanistan.

"I think Kazakhstan is well-positioned to do this as Russia and some other states are not correctly perceived here," he said in a clear reference to Moscow's ill-fated intervention from Afghanistan in 1979-1989.
